sources.entry: Finicky - Always opens the right browser.

summary.one_liner: Finicky is a macOS default-browser app that routes each clicked URL to a browser or app chosen by user-written JavaScript or TypeScript rules.
summary.what_it_does: Finicky runs as the default browser on macOS and decides, for each URL, which browser or application should open it. Rules live in a JavaScript or TypeScript config file at ~/.finicky.js, with a defaultBrowser fallback, match-based handlers, and rewrite rules. Rewrite rules can edit URLs before they open, for example forcing HTTPS or changing a host. Matching supports glob-style patterns, regular expressions, and custom functions. Browser extensions for Chrome and Firefox add an "open with Finicky" option and let alt-click send links to Finicky directly.
use_cases: route links to different browsers by site
open work and personal links in separate browsers
force HTTPS on links before opening
set a default browser that picks per-URL targets
open social or meeting links in a specific app
how_to_run: Or download the app from the releases page
Create ~/.finicky.js (JavaScript or TypeScript) with a default browser and handlers, using the example config or example-config folder as a template
Start Finicky from Applications or Spotlight/Alfred/Raycast and allow it to be set as the default browser
Launching Finicky manually opens the configuration/troubleshooting window
notable: Per-URL browser routing configured in plain JavaScript or TypeScript
URL rewriting before a link is opened, such as host changes or HTTPS enforcement
Regex and custom function matching in addition to glob patterns
Browser extensions for Chrome and Firefox that send links to Finicky
Migration guide from Finicky 3 provided in the wiki
caveats: Requires setting Finicky as the default browser and writing a config file by hand
Detailed configuration docs are in the external wiki rather than the README
